issues.quote: He had been four years on that watch and he played it for anyone who would sit still.
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives no duration for the uncle's repeater or its ownership.
issues.misreading: A solver could read 'four years' as a timing clue or as a duration linked to the night's events, and could also read 'on that watch' as the uncle having owned or worked on the watch for four years.

issues.quote: It has given me trouble for ten years and I have never let anyone near it, my uncle included.
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives no duration for the nephew's watch trouble.
issues.misreading: The number 'ten' here could be confused with the ten o'clock strike or the ten slow notes of the repeater, pulling attention toward the wrong clock reading.

issues.quote: I had a glass of brandy, then another.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says only that he went up to the library after dinner, stayed there alone, and heard ten strike. It gives no drinking or time spent there.
issues.misreading: The brandy detail, and later 'I finished the brandy', could suggest a duration of time spent in the library or a reason for lapses in attention, which the sheet does not support.
